title: Observability
description:
This course covers the fundamentals of observability in distributed systems. Today, Kubernetes has become the de facto standard for Cloud Native applications and is widely used for distributed systems. To be effective as an observability expert, it is critical to understand how to monitor and respond to the health and performance of both your Kubernetes clusters and the applications hosted on them. This course will teach students how to collect system performance data using Prometheus, how to collect application tracing data using Jaeger, and how to visualize the results in a dashboard using Grafana.Introduction to Cloud Observability
In this first lesson, we'll go over the big picture. Why is observability relevant? And what is your role is as an observability engineer? What tools will you need to be able to conduct observability?
 Observability Tools
This lesson will get you set up with Prometheus, Jaeger, and Grafana, the main tools you need to start doing observability in your cluster.
 SLOs, SLIs, and Error Budgets
In order to observe performance, we first need to get clear on how we are defining and measuring it. We'll do this using Service-Level Objectives and Service-Level Indicators.
 Tracing
Tracing will allow us to get performance data on our applications, particularly on the latency of the key processes within them. In this lesson, we'll learn how to conduct tracing using Jaeger.
 Building Dashboards
We'll look at how we can use Grafana to visualize the data we've been collecting, so that we can see the performance of our system and application at a glance.

title: Embedded Systems: Sensor Integration and Communication
description:
This course covers sensor integration and communication protocols. You will learn about different types of sensors, including external and ultrasonic sensors, and their interfacing techniques. The course also teaches essential communication protocols for effective data transmission. By the end of this course, you will be equipped to implement and manage sensor-based systems in embedded applications.Introduction to Sensors
Explore sensor basics, types like environmental & motion, how they measure changes & importance in automation, healthcare, and environmental monitoring.
 External Sensors
Explore external sensors' role, advantages, and trade-offs for system integration, including considerations like accuracy, cost, and environmental impact.
 Ultrasonic Measurements
Discover ultrasonic measurement: principles, HC-SR04 sensor operation, interfacing with ESP32, limitations, and real-world applications.

title: Applying AI to 2D Medical Imaging Data
description:
Introduction to AI for 2D Medical Imaging
In this lesson, you will be given an introduction to this course about AI for 2D medical imaging, why AI is important and where AI fits in the space.
 Clinical Foundations of 2D Medical Imaging
In this lesson, we will cover clinical foundations such as clinical workflows, applications of 2D imaging in clinical settings and how machine learning impacts clinics.
 2D Medical Imaging Exploratory Data Analysis
In this lesson, we will learn the DICOM standard in medical imaging, and how to explore medical imaging data and prepare it for machine learning applications.
 Classification Models of 2D Medical Images
In this lesson, we'll dive deep into classification tasks for 2D medical imaging using different machine learning models. and we will talk about pre-process data, train, test, and validate models.
 Translating AI Algorithms for Clinical Settings with the FDA
In this lesson, you will learn about how your work fits into the bigger picture, and how it’s regulated by the FDA, which is an often-overlooked, but incredibly important.

title: Applying AI to 3D Medical Imaging Data
description:
Introduction to AI for 3D Medical Imaging
In this lesson, we will introduce the course and instructors. We will give you an overview of the context for AI in 3D medical imaging space, and cover the objectives of the course.
 3D Medical Imaging - Clinical Fundamentals
In this lesson, we cover the basic terminology and concepts related to 3D medical imaging. We will look at the problem space from a clinical standpoint and learn how CT and MR scanners produce images.
 3D Imaging Exploratory Data Analysis
In this lesson, we will dive deeper into medical imaging formats NIFTI and DICOM, how scanner data is represented, and how to read medical volumes stored in these files and analyze them.
 3D Medical Imaging - End-to-End Deep Learning Applications
In this lesson, we cover the basics of building deep neural networks for 3D medical imaging (mostly segmentation & classification) and performance evaluation from a software and clinical perspective.
 Deploying AI Algorithms in Real World Scenarios
In this lesson, we'll talk about clinical networks, architecture, and AI deployment, tools and their use by data scientists and clinicians, as well as medical device regulation and data privacy.

title: Applying AI to EHR Data
description:
With the transition to electronic health records (EHR) over the last decade, the amount of EHR data has increased exponentially, providing an incredible opportunity to unlock this data with AI to benefit the healthcare system. Learn the fundamental skills of working with EHR data in order to build and evaluate compliant, interpretable machine learning models that account for bias and uncertainty using cutting-edge libraries and tools including Tensorflow Probability, Aequitas, and Shapley. Understand the implications of key data privacy and security standards in healthcare. Apply industry code sets, transform datasets at different EHR data levels, and use Tensorflow to engineer features.Applying AI to EHR Data Introduction
This lesson will provide you with an Introduction to the EHR Data course outline, content, as well as introduce you to your instructor.
 EHR Data Security and Analysis
In this lesson, you will learn about the importance of data security and the different standards that apply to EHR, as well as analyzing EHR data.
 EHR Code Sets
In this lesson you will learn how to work with different EHR codes and how to map them properly to records.
 EHR Transformations & Feature Engineering
In this lesson, you'll gain skills in feature engineering and transformation of EHR.
 Building, Evaluating and Interpreting Models
In this final lesson, you'll be putting all of your skills together to build, evaluate and interpret ML models for Bias and Uncertainty.

title: Applying AI to Wearable Device Data
description:
Introduction to Wearable Data
We’ll cover what wearables are and the scope of the class. Learn who your instructor is and his thoughts on the promise and caveats of wearables in medical research and decision making.
 Intro to Digital Sampling & Signal Processing
A brief tour through sampling theory, signal processing, the Fourier transform, and other related topics. We’ll briefly cover some plotting and visualization techniques here as well.
 Introduction to Sensors
We cover the basics of the accelerometer, the PPG sensor, and the ECG sensor, as well as what these signals look like in typical environments and the types of noise that we will encounter.
 Activity Classification
Build an activity classifier using a wrist-worn accelerometer!
 ECG Signal Processing
We deep dive into a fundamental algorithm for ECG processing and use that as the basis for an arrhythmia detection algorithm.

title: Cybersecurity for Business Leaders
description:
This course will give business leaders the foundation they need to initiate discussions around cybersecurity. We will explore the current landscape of threats and look at ways to defend against attacks by investing in technology and culture, but also by being proactive in your risk management planning.Cyber Challenges We Face Today
Learn about what threats are, types of threats, where they originate, and how they attack. You will also look at your biggest vulnerability: your people.
 Effective Detection and Response
Learn how a combination of people, policy, and technology is used to detect and respond to threats and attacks.
 Cybersecurity Culture
The culture of any organization is shaped by leadership; Learn how to practice and promote an organizational culture that embraces cybersecurity.
 Making Investments
An organization’s cybersecurity posture is only as effective as the investments made into cybersecurity. Learn how to think about talent, risk, and budget.
 (Elective) Threat Analysis by Industry
In this lesson, we look at the cybersecurity landscape of the technology industry, healthcare industry, and finance industry.

The rapidly evolving nature of these technologies, especially with the increasing use of AI, is revolutionizing industries and bringing automation to previously unthinkable areas. There is  the involvement  of numerous factors  that make these nutrients available  tp plants. These include  enviromental  conditions ,  microorganisms  and soil organisms. Nutrients  are recycled. These are important  to determine the health status  of plants  via the measurement of nutrients  in the enviroment. Other parameters  include pH and conductivity . These are important  to adjust  the amount of nutrients  required  by plants.
1. The elements and their relationship  to plants  2. Soil - plant - atmosphere  distribution of nutrients  3. Use of nutrients  with minimal harmful effects on the enviroment. 1. description:

title: Award in Sports Fitness Nutrition
Foundation Certificate in Care
description:
This programme of studies is aimed at those individuals who wish to embark on a future career in the Health and Social Care Sector. During the year the learners will have a variety of lectures which will give them an understanding of basic concepts related to this sector. Lectures will focus on human behaviour,  the way the body works and what constitutes a safe working environment. Learners will also be given the opportunity to strengthen their key skills subjects including Maltese,  English,  Mathematics and Science through the vocational perspective. Learners will have the opportunity to visit organisations related to this sector so that they become accustomed to the environment.
Understand human biology and behavioural science principles underpinning the delivery of health and social care Explore the health and social care needs of different services user groups and the basic skills required to deliver health and social care services Develop awareness of health and safety issues in the delivery of health and social care to provide a safe working environment for the service user and the carer. Understand the breadth of service user groups in health and social care and the range of care settings

title: VET Award in Process Manufacturing
description:
Provides the learner with the required numeracy,  operational English  and English and basic IT skills to work effectively in process manufacturing. By the end of this course the learner will gain the ability to operate safely  manufacturing machinery and tools by following the Occupational Health and Safety standards. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able  to follow the correct technical processes used in accordance to the task being assigned.
Describe  how to correctly calculate single/two digit multiplications and divisions.  Define  how decimals are used to measure. Recite the appropriate action verbs in the past,  present and future simple tense in a given context. Write a  simple sentence by using basic English words. Describe the typical use of the desktop PC,  laptop and  touch screen devices and adjust the main computer settings. List some of the main output devices such as screens/monitors,  printers,  scanners,  memory drives (pen drives),  and WI-FI route. Describe the Occupational Health and Safety procedures at the workplace. Name the hazards and risks associated with workplace activities,  including housekeeping. Recite organisational policies,  mission statement,  cultural values and behaviours that encompass punctuality,  work ethics and teamwork. Quote company manufacturing standard operating procedures and work instructions. Quote the organization’s Mission and Quality Policy Statements. Identify the organizational standard operating procedures to obtain products of the requisite quality and in accordance with industrial and regulatory standards. Demonstrate  how to round up numbers. Demonstrate  how to use a calculator,  including its basic functions correctly. Use basic manufacturing vocabulary and basic technical terminology pertaining to a manufacturing context. Operate in a process manufacturing context by being able to read and understand organisational procedures,  policies,  technical and work instructions written in English,  correctly.  Show how to start a computer and log on/off  securely using a user name and password. Use the main types of software such as: operating systems and applications in a process manufacturing context. Practise the identification and communication of Near Miss incidents and accidents in accordance with organisational procedures. Use and maintain the appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) for the tasks at hand. Practise manufacturing tasks based on job cards,  company’s blueprints,  bills of materials and other technical documentation. Demonstrate the handling of materials and products in accordance with organizational instructions,  including segregation and labelling specifications. Operate effectively within  the team to enable the company to offer products of the highest quality. Operate in an orderly and logical manner to minimise the risk of confusion between different products or their components,  to avoid cross-contamination and to minimise the risk of omission or wrong application of any of the manufacturing or control steps.

•	Use tools, equipment and machine safely and appropriately depending on the material
•	Demonstrate correct manufacturing and assembly processes through safe handling of machinery
•	Use the correct timber for a given task
•	Show how to finish off and clean up after a given task

description:
This course addresses the significant need of customer care aptitude in the current economic situation which stresses excellence in customer care service.
Develop effective communication skills to succeed in Customer service. Practice empathy and assertiveness when problem solving. Exhibit good listening skills to understand the customers' needs. Use appropriate telephone techniques. Have basic knowledge of the field of Customer Care. Appreciate the significant possibilities and the diverse employment areas related to Customer Care. Effectively deal with customer complaints, angry customers. Appreciate the role and importance of internal customers. Carry out with responsibility and autonomy simple tasks related to Customer care

title: Award in Care Work - We Care!
description:
The purpose of this module is to provide an introduction to the field of care,  and the jobs of care workers whose main aim is to help vulnerable people to manage their daily activities and to live as independently as possible. It aims to cover basic health and safety practices,  social interaction and ethical practices required of the caregiver. With this foundation module learners can be confident of their ability to embark on,  and continue further studies in,  this field
Use appropriate tone,  language and terminology with clients and  stakeholders. Identify barriers to communication and practice strategies to address these barriers. Assess own strengths and areas requiring personal development with regards to the skills and knowledge needed to work successfully within a team. Demonstrate an understanding of the skills needed to improve one’s communication skills with clients. Discover ways to keep oneself updated and constantly renew  acquired skills.

title: Authorised Gas Tester Level 2 Award
description:
The purpose of this programme is to provide the learner with a brief background  to the requirements of the gas testing procedure and confined space entry procedure.  It will also provide a necessary understanding of the basics of hazard management of oxygen enriched/ deficient,  toxic and flammable gas atmospheres.  It will enhance the learners competency and ability to identify atmospheres that may be immediately dangerous to life or health.
Interact with others so as to coordinate site safety before  work in a confined space; Interact with others so as to coordinate site safety when work is being done that could generate hazardous fumes; Proceed to identify  various types of gas monitors; Proceed to check an area for  hazardous gasses by means of gas monitor; Proceed to check an area for low oxygen concentration; Proceed to activate an emergency plan in case of an emergency; The step taken to call for help and phone 112; Proceed to relay essential information to the emergency services; Proceed to take control of situation and delegate responsibilities. Describe when an Gas monitor  should be used; Explain the safety precautions one should take; in analysing air  before entering a confined space; State the limitations of gas monitors; State the dangers of low oxygen; Describe the effects of various dangerous gasses; Report and maintain records of findings and actions carried out; Explain how to set up he relevant dedector for each gas testing aplicaiton,  its potential failure modes and confirming its correct functioning; Undertake further studies so as to gain information and knowledge on how to use an Gas monitor; Study the precautions that need to be taken when using an gas monitor

title: Award in Customer Care- The Customer is Always Right!
description:
This course provides students with tools to help them reflect on their own skills and equip them with the fundamental skills necessary to enter the workplace in a customer service role. All organisations in the service industry have a need for people with quality customer service skills,  and this course aims to build learners confidence by utilising concepts learnt,  and empower them to feel they can confidently add this to their skill set.
Choose the appropriate tone of voice,  words,  and body language expected when serving customers in the workplace. Apply jargon related to the customer service field.  Apply a service mindset to deliver optimal service Assess strengths and areas for further personal development in line with delivery of customer service. Develop one’s sense of personal worth.

title: Award in Health and Safety and Planning Procedures in Marine and Diving Works
description:
Participants will acquire knowledge about safe diving practices to be adopted in operations in which persons are employed to work underwater. Participants will acquire competencies about safe marine and diving works and related supporting safe work practices conducted in connection with all types of work in a marine environment, for land-based construction work carried out on, adjacent to or over water and underwater.
Demonstrate an understanding of potential hazards in marine-related workplaces and appropriate responses. Apply health and safety procedures in marine-related workplaces. Demonstrate an understanding of how to comply with regulations concerning health and safety in the marine environment at the national level and how follow the best practices that are used at the international level in this particular work environment. Define the responsibilities of employees,  contractors and supervisors working in marine-related sectors. Become acquainted with diving modes and competences of divers. Be acquainted with procedures and permits to work are required in a port area and in places close to the shore but outside the designated port areas. Define safety planning requirements on a marine-related workplace. Identify warning symbols and safety signs related to health and safety in marine-related workplaces.

title: Award in Customer Care and Sales Techniques
description:
This programme is designed to raise awareness on the methods in which positive customer relationships are kept and customer concerns dealt with. The learners will also be exposed to a number of sales techniques and after-sales strategies designed to upskill the learners and contribute to customers’ overall positive experience.
a) Apply their knowledge of the customer life-cycle in different contexts.
b) Demonstrate appropriate identification of individualised customer needs. 
c) Apply the appropriate communication approach required as per customer needs.
d) Implement positive stress management techniques.
c) Demonstrate professionalism and assertiveness across various scenarios. 
d) Apply effective and persuasive sales techniques.
e) Practice of sales techniques across different customer profiles.
f) Apply effective after-sales care methods appropriate to the customer’s needs. a)  Ensure the application of good customer relationship management strategies and techniques learnt.
b) Collaborate with colleagues to ensure positive stress management 
c) Create and maintain professionalism throughout interactions with customers.
c) Produce and carry out effective sales strategies appropriate to the customer’s needs.
d) Deal with after-sales customer care, applying a positive and professional approach to customer complaints and requests. a) Define and recall the 5 different stages of the customer lifecycle:
     - Awareness
     - Consideration
     - Purchase
     - Retention
     - Advocacy
b) Describe the importance of client relationship management (CRM) to an organisation.
c) Define the main 4 different communication styles as well as identify and describe one’s own (learner’s own) communication style. 
d) Describe 5 stress management techniques; Identify and apply at least 2 such technique that are appropriate and beneficial to the individual learner in the context of maintaining positive customer relationships.
e) Define and describe the components that make-up a professional approach with customers.
f) Define and recall 5 successful sales techniques.
g) Identify appropriate sales techniques to match different customer profiles.
h) Identify and describe approaches and strategies related to handling of complaints as part of after-sales care with customers.

title: Foundation Certificate in Sport
description:
This programme of studies serves as a stepping stone to a future working career in the sport sector. The learner experiences the practical and basic theoretical components of a number of sports and fitness related subjects. The vocational studyunits cover the basics of health and active lifestyles,  community sports,  fitness training methods and include an introduction to gym-based exercise. Concurrently,  learners strengthen their knowledge of the key skills in English,  Maltese,  Mathematics,  Science,  Information Technology,  and Individual and Social Responsibility. Throughout the academic year,  MCAST and the Institute of Community Services organise a number of sport related extra-curricular activities in which the learners will be invited to participate in order to enrich their experience on campus.
Consider and promote a healthy and active lifestyle Identify and manage health stressors and administer basic first aid in a sports environment Control and monitor development of fitness using appropriate testing procedures. Demonstrate safe and effective exercise techniques and become familiar with a gym environment

title: VET Award for Cleaning Attendants
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work in the cleaning industry,  or wishes to progress within his/ her existing cleaning profession. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to identify and understand which particular cleaning method is used in accordance to the task being assigned.
Be Familiar with the importance of feeling empowered at the place of work. Understand the importance of effective communication in a professional context. Know how to count,  read,  write and rank positive numbers. Understand ratio and proportions. Attain sound knowledge on the colour coding system,  hand hygiene procedure and the PH indicator. Understand the different cleaning techniques used for general cleaning.  Understand the various individual cleaning techniques used in accordance to the numerous industry related cleaning specifications. Demonstrate how to interpret and translate the information listed on a standard cleaning frequenncy sheet,  so as to ensure proper completion. Apply a sense of empowerment to a cleaner's role. Apply general health and safety principles to ensure a safe workplace. Demonstrate the correct procedure needed to handle basic first aid interventions. Show good working practices. Apply the best method to work out simple work related calculations in relation to volume and area. Demonsrate proper use of equations and formulas so as to ensure effective cleaning. Build confidence when using heavy duty cleaning machines. Use the correct cleaning tools according to the task at hand. Apply the correct cleaning approach according to the industry requirements. Demonstrate confidence in knowing the correct cleaning procedure to be used.

title: Award in Assistant Limestone Block and Hollow Concrete Block Layer
description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety working practices; acquire knowledge to be able to assist in the identification of systems,  equipment and components; develop knowledge and skills to be able to assist in reading of drawings and calculations with approved procedures and under supervision; and to be knowledgeable and have the skill of assisting in the laying of limestone and hollow concrete blocks to line.
Assist in the identification of systems,  equipment and components. Assist in reading of drawings and calculations. Communicate with fellow workers. Read method statements and safe works preventive measures. Apply occupational health and safety during work practices. Assist in the  laying of limestone and hollow concrete blocks to line. Implement actions as per method statements and safe work practices

title: Award in Customer Care
description:
The course addresses  the significant need of customer care aptitude in the current economic situation which  stresses excellence in customer care  service
Knowledge,  Skills and Competences  At the end of the course the learner is expected to demonstrate basic competency in Customer Care skills with some independence and autonomy. This will include: Knowledge:  a)Being aware and responsive to the policies and procedures of the specific work area. b)Appreciating the role of internal customers. c)Measure the service against that of competitors. Skills: a)Offering the best possible service to customers in a professional manner.  b)Exhibiting good listening skills to understand the customers’ needs. c)Working as part of a team in order to provide the customer with the best possible service. d)Using appropriate telephone techniques e)Developing effective communication skills to succeed in Customer Service.  Competences: a)Practicing empathy and assertiveness when problem solving. b)Being competent in dealing with customers’ complaints. c)Show competence in dealing with angry customersd)Continuously collect feedback from customers to improve service

title: VET Award  Foundation in Oxy Acetylene Welding and Cutting
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to gain employment as an Oxy-Acetylene Welder. Through this training programme,  the learner will review OHS requirements for welding environments and be able select suitable techniques to produce basic welded joints including Gas Cutting using Oxy-Acetylene welding technology.
Quote health and safety principles and regulations for working with Oxy-Acetylene Welding equipment. Describe health and safety measures and precautions to prevent hazards and to ensure the safety of oneself and third parties when working with Oxy-Acetylene Welding equipment. Describe the procedures and processes to weld beads on a steel plate in the flat position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding. Describe the procedures and processes to weld Lap Fillet Joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding. Demonstrate knowledge of typical basic non destructive testing procedures used by the industry to check welds. Use industry standard techniques to check a weld for visual defeats. Practice welding Tee Fillet Joints in the flat position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding. Practice welding Tee Fillet Joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Oxy-Acetylene Welding.

title: Award as Assistant Tile Layer
Fire Safety and Related Emergencies
description:
This course is designed to raise awareness on fire hazards and train participants on how to act safely in the event of an emergency fire situation.
A sound understanding of the role,  functions and responsibility of a fire marshal; Ability to identify which are the elements that need to be present for a fire to occurs,  the three basic principles of fire extinction and the principles and practice of fire risk analysis; Ability to identify the key elements for effective fire risk management in the workplace; Knowledge of the use of various types of fire equipment; An understanding of the correct methods of fire prevention measures that can be taken to minimize fire hazards; Knowledge of common types of evacuation procedures and the control of personnel; Knowledge of all categories of fire signage,  according to the type of message they are intended to convey Follow fire prevention good practices; Determine the type of approach needed to properly apply fire safety procedures for every workplace; Understand the importance of teamwork in an emergency situation; Apply fire control measures to manage fire inherent and residual risks; Cooperate with co-workers and health & safety representatives in the event of an emergency in any workplace. Adequately apply organisational & prioritizing skills in emergency situations. Identify and be able to use fire fighting equipment (extinguishers,  hydrants fire signage,  smoke alarms fire blanket and personal fire protection equipment). Instruct personnel to prevent basic and arson fire prevention. Observe,  receive and obtain information to complete an incident report form. Implement risk analysis in the workplace and be able to manage these risks. Implement measures to protect all workers,  colleagues and clients. Identify the safety fire equipment available and manage the safe use of portable fire-fighting equipment. Manage emergency procedures and the control of personnel

description:
The course will provide the learner with a brief background  to the requirements of the Gas testing procedure and confined space entry procedure.  Provide the necessary understanding of the basics of hazard management of oxygen enriched/ deficient,  toxic and flammable gas atmospheres.  It will enhance the learners competency and ability to identify atmospheres that me be immediately dangerous to life or health.
The learner will be able to: To furthers ones knowledge on the use of portable gas tester; To furtherones knowledge on air testing; To further ones knowledge on the use of portable gas tester; To develop the use of relevent information and furhter knowledge in practical skills when analysing air in a confined space; Understand the narcotic effects of hydrocarbons; To furhter ones knowledge in gas testing for hot work and confined spaces. The learner will be able to:  Effective use of a portable gas monitor to test and area and to Interpret and document the results of gas testing.

title: Award in Assistant Demolition Operative
description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with sound knowledge of occupational health and safety working practices and acquire the competence to be able to assist to operate handheld power tools and equipment in the workplace within the building and construction sector. The candidate shall cover procedures and principles on how to assist in demolition and dismantling of existing structures manually (by hand) under supervision on construction sites.
Learning to learn how to keep updated with the content learned during the course. Communicate with colleagues and supervisors or site managers. Communicate using simple glossary terms used in the building and construction. Communicate using basic Maltese or English. Use appropriate nonverbal communication

title: Award in Health and Safety at the Workplace
description:
Aimed at providing basic knowledge to health and safety, including minimizing risk of injury, accident prevention, and other ways to improve safety at the workcation and support on construction sites.
The learner will be able to: 

- Ability to understand, interpret and apply health and safety regulation.
- Assess risk and provide consultancy on mitigating it.
- Lead individuals to a healthier and safer environment through consultancy and raising awareness of health and safety on 
  construction sites.
- Provide health and safety reports.
- Resolve disputes and improve the work environment. The learner will be able to: 

- Prevent health and safety hazards
- Understand better work environment
-Use of health and safety equipment
- Appropriately manage incidents at work place The learner will be able to: 

- Provide insight in the health and safety report
- Train on how to approach individuals who require health and safety support
- Report writing
- Basic knowledge of fire and first aid.

title: Award in Common Health and Safety Issues: Occupational Risk for Lone Workers,  Young Workers and Workers in Hot and Cold Environments
description:
The course is designed to provide participants with the knowledge and awareness of specific hazards at workplace: heat and cold stress (temperature at which work becomes dangerous),  lone working (a person who works alone) and safety risks for young worker (a person under eighteen years of age who works).
Report properly all accidents,  injuries,  near-misses and other dangerous occurrences. Identify correct health and safety procedures connected with the type of working practice when someone is working alone. An understanding of the importance of personal safety for lone workers. Knowledge of the risks that a person may face as a lone worker and ways to reduce these risks. An understanding of how cooperate among workers to improve safety and health’ procedures in circumstances involving lone labours.

title: Award in Basic Tile Laying Techniques
description:
The training course is intended to give the necessary knowledge, skills and competences to someone wishing to work in the building and construction sector. It is specifically focusing on basic tile laying knowledge and skills.
Outline the preventative and remedial actions to be taken in the case of exposure to materials hazardous to health. Report any hazards which may present risk to relevant persons. Assist and perform installation of tiles under supervision. Confirm that all materials, tools and equipment necessary for the installation process are available as required. Confirm that all material, tools and equipment are fit for their intended purpose. Understand and explain the correct procedure for setting out work systems. Identify instances where additional information would be necessary and liaise with supervisor accordingly. Look for information, directions and guidance in the use of materials and tools

title: Award in Common Health and Safety Issues: Occupational Risk for Lone Workers, Young Workers and Workers in Hot and Cold Environments
description:
The course is designed to provide participants with the knowledge and awareness of specific hazards at workplace: heat and cold stress (temperature at which work becomes dangerous), lone working (a person who works alone) and safety risks for young worker (a person under eighteen years of age who works).
Report properly all accidents, injuries, near-misses and other dangerous occurrences. Identify correct health and safety procedures connected with the type of working practice when someone is working alone. An understanding of the importance of personal safety for lone workers. Knowledge of the risks that a person may face as a lone worker and ways to reduce these risks. An understanding of how cooperate among workers to improve safety and health’ procedures in circumstances involving lone labours.

title: General Education Award in Spanish II
description:
By the end of this instructional course,  the learner will be able to acquire good knowledge in Spanish expressions,  grammar,  sentence structure and communicate with ease. This level is intended to bridge the existing gap between MQF levl 1 and Adavanced level which is pegged at MQF level 3 .

title: Award in Provision  for Cleaning Services
description:
This course is specifically designed taking into account the limitations of persons employed in the industry in terms of learning capabilities and an extremely interactive approach shall be undertaken,  with the trainer having been involved in the cleaning industry for years and owning one of the major cleaning companies in Malta. To this effect,  the students shall be embracing first-hand experience with regards to both the theoratical aspect of the course and with continuous hands-on experience reflecting the theoretical parts of the course.
1. Be conversant with the basic theoratical and practical aspects of health and safety in the cleaning industry 2. Attain basic knowledge of chemical handling 3. Identify the correct to use of cleaning machinery  4. Recognise  the importance of COSHH regulations (Control Substances Hazardous to Health) 5. Show an understanding of the use of colour codes 6. Understand the problems with cross contamination 7. Be proficient in the understanding of the difference between cleaning,  disinfection and decontamination 8. Recognise the importance of correct storage of equipment and machinery. 1. Perform general duties relating to cleaning 2. Follow good working practise in relation to use of equipment and machinery 3. Determine the type of approach needed with regards to cleaning,  disinfection and decontamination 4. Access or request to all sources of information relating to COSHH regulations (Control of Subsances Hazardous to Health). 5. Provide suitable solutions for avoidance of cross contamination 6. Follow good working practices relating to correct storage of equipment and machinery 7. Access or request to sources of information relating to colour codes 8.Follow good working practices with regards to chemical handling 9. Establish clients requirements in such a manner that bridges the relationship between the employer and the client 10. Communicate and maintain a dialogue with the supervisors at work when necessary and on an ongoing basis 11. Assess which work practice is the most adequate in terms of health and safety  12. Learn both  the theoratical and practical necessities for performing the job description correctly.

title: Award in Waste Collection and Transportation of Waste
description:
Transport and disposal of municipal solid waste is one of the major environmental problems. Improper transport and disposal of municipal solid waste causes hazards to inhabitants. The amount of solid waste generated is steadily increasing and every government in this world is currently focusing on methods to approach the challenge. This unit develops good awareness of recycling activities and key statutory requirements. In addition,  learners will be more skilled at organising their workspace,  working practices and resources as well as working more effectively with each other as a team. Overall,  they will acquire the skills necessary to work more safely and efficiently.
Understand ways of mitigating potential impacts during the collection and transport of waste. Environmental Impact of Waste Management. Regulatory Policy and Legislation. Understanding the principles and procedures for waste transfer activities. Identify types of waste and arising in the Maltese Islands and relevant stakeholders. Health and Safety in the collection and handling of waste.

title: Award in Safe Use of Electrical Hand Held Apparatus
description:
This course is designed for those workers who need to work on electrical equipment who either have no electrical qualifications or need a reminder of electrical dangers and safe working practices. This course provides knowledge and skills on electrical and mechanical hazards,  on the functioning of portable tools and on the safety procedures to use at workplace.
Perform a basic risk assessment to identify the hazards specific to electrical safety,  the risks arising from those hazards,  and the control measures you should use.Achieve a visual inspection that should be carried out by the user each and every time the equipment is used,  checking for example for evidence of damage,  loose cables etc. Determine the type of approach needed to comply with safe work procedure. Apply procedures of operational maintenance. Cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives in the organisation of an electrical emergency in workplace. Know the general site safety,  particularly from the point of view of electrical hazards. Understand the electrical and mechanical hazards that can be encountered using an electrical tool and the precautions to be taken. Know technical and organisational preventive measures relevant to electrical and mechanical hazards in the use of electrical hand held apparatus. Know how identify and report faulty portable electrical equipment and withdraw it from service,  by ensuring it cannot be used and/or is marked faulty.

title: Award in Health and Safety
description:
The aim of this module is to provide learners with the basic health and safety knowledge and skill requirements
The learner will be able to: a) Understand health and safety requirementsb) Identify risks and hazards The Elements of the law Advantages and disadvantages of the law History of occupational health and safety Hazards caused by fire Learning the recovery position Treatment to chocking Treatment to electrical shock Sprains and strains First aid box Electrical safety Classes of fire and fire extinguishers Safety signs Health and Safety responsibilities of the employer Powers of officers

title: Foundation Certificate in Applied Science
description:
This programme of studies is aimed at giving learners the opportunity to further their studies in several diverse sciencerelated areas including environmental,  health and industrial sciences. Learners will cover various topics such as Chemistry,  Physics,  Biology,  English,  Maltese,  Mathematics and IT which will be taught in an applied manner that is relevant to the various science sectors in which employment may be sought with a higher qualification. This programme is particularly suitable for learners who have a scientific or technical aptitude,  even if they have not decided fully on their ultimate career choice.
Understand some of the factors that influence scientific progress. Describe the main factors that affect the health of individuals Make accurate scientific observations and measurements in given situations Understand what skills and qualities are required for jobs in the science sector

title: Award in Organic Farming
description:
This course will give applicants a general introduction in organic farming. Learners will understand that organic farming entails a holistic approach towards the production of food and production without compromising the future generation of production. Organic farming is sustainable and it promotes the welfare of animals. The principles of care, fairness, health and ecology are enhanced while the methods and practices applied leads to the production of food without any residues of synthetic preservatives. The philosophy of organic agriculture is against genetically modified organisms. Regards the rearing of animals no antibiotics or growth hormones are allowed on the farm. This introduction course will instill insight in the learners to comprehend, appreciate and understand organic farming and provide them with the necessary skills to start their own organic business.
Manage a horticultural unit and a poultry unit Apply a holistic approach towards organic production by embracing the principles of ecology, health, fairness and care Convert from conventional to organic practices

title: Award in Working in Low Risk Confined Spaces
description:
The objective of this programme is for those learners already working or preparing to work in industry or in any organisation where they can be exposed to confined spaces such as during construction work etc.
Topics covered in this course are regarded by the Health & safety authority  as being important in maintaining good practice in the safe, prompt and effective prevention of injuries that are in most cases fatal. The qualification provides learners with the knowledge, understanding and skills in working safely in confined spaces – medium risk
•	State the role and responsibilities for an individual carrying out work in confined space
•	Proceed to assess a task, and  select the proper rescue  equipment to use
•	Proceed to implement the emergency plan  following an incident
•	Ability to select proper PPE
•	Proceed to select the type of portable gas monitor needed for task at hand
•	Proceed to select a proper respiratory protection
•	Proceed to carry out a risk assessment and develop a rescue plan
•	State the steps to be taken to call for help and phone 112
•	Describe the safe use of a tripod  and winch used to recue injured workers
•	Describe the safe use of a  portable gas monitor
•	Describe the hazards of confined spaces
•	Describe the importance of the work permit
•	Undertake further studies so as to gain information and knowledge on working in confined spaces
•	Name and describe the effects of  the most common hazardous gasses that could be resent in confined spaces
•	Describe the effects of low oxygen concentrations
•	Describe the use and limits of various types of respiratory protection
•	Discuss with others the working procedures
•	Discuss the limitations and the appropriate application of  injured worker retrieval system
•	Discuss the fundamental components of a rescue system
•	Discuss the appropriate location and use of a tripod
•	Discuss the importance of manufacturer’s recommendations when using a portable gas monitor.
•	Discuss the limits of a gas monitor
•	Discuss IDLH atmospheres 
•	Discuss the roles and responsibilities of employers, supervisors and workers in regards to a f rescue plan and emergency procedures
Further one`s knowledge on  the importance of health surveillance and the undergoing of regular medical check ups to check fitness for the job •	Be able to list typical accidents and injuries related to working in confined spaces in the workplace
•	Be able to provide instruction to others re actions to be taken in a given situation.
•	Promote proper interaction with others so as to coordinate help during an accident.
•	Promote proper interaction  with others so as to coordinate and prepare a work plan
•	Provide suitable care and maintenance to equipment
•	Demonstrate competence in carrying out a proper work risk assessment
•	Demonstrate competence in carrying out visual inspection for equipment
•	Demonstrate competence in monitoring air quality by means of a portable gas / air tester
•	Reports and maintain records of findings and actions carried out during equipment visual inspections.
•	Convey proper information to other professionals, site supervisors etc.

title: Award in Basic English for Care Workers
description:
The objective is to help those who work in the care industry,  for whom English is not their first language,  to communicate better in a healthcare setting by improving their spoken communication,  vocabulary,  grammar and pronunciation.  An important aspect of this course will be the input of language  skills which do not necessarily pertain specifically to the caring environment but will be useful in the circumstances.
Participate in and understand the main points of discussions/explanations/instructions with potential colleagues. Interact with clients and their relatives in the course of their duties. Communicate information in a clear manner. Explain how to select an appropriate method of communication for different situations. Use the auxiliary verbs be and have got in positive,  negative and question form. Demonstrate sentence structure (positive,  negative and question form). Compose positive and negative sentences using present,  past and future tenses. . Apply appropriate vocabulary related to colours,  numbers,  food,  health,  clothes,  leisure activities,  family,  parts of the body,  likes/dislikes and express feelings. Express oneself using comparative and superlative structures. Use relevant prepositions (time/place/movement) where necessary. Use countable and uncountable nouns. Use personal pronouns in both a grammatical and lexical context.  Identify terms of address or age appropriate words and phrases depending on client groups and relatives’ state of emotion. Construct ‘Wh’ sentence question forms using present,  past and future tenses. Talk about ability using can/can’t. Express advice through the use of must/mustn’t,  do/don’t,  should/shouldn’t,  need to and don’t need  to. Use of imperative structures,  Tell the time and refer to the calendar (days/months).  Understand how to communicate effectively by using the correct grammar and punctuation in a social care setting.

title: Award in Beauty Therapy - Introduction
description:
This course covers a basic knowledge about beauty therapy with the scope of helping participants realize if they want to become internationally qualified Beauty Therapists.
It is also aimed at those who help out in a Beauty Salon and are relatives of a Beauty Salon owner – this course gives participants a good idea of the different aspects of basic Beauty Therapy.
Identify which clients are able to receive beauty treatments Describe the anatomy and physiology related to the skin Perform basic applications carried out in a beauty salon

title: Award in Customer  Relationship  and Communication

title: Award in Medical Maltese (Part 2)
description:
This course is offered to BARTS University registered students aiming to work or are working/practicing in the health profession whose mother tongue is not Maltese and would like to ascertain an elementary to pre-intermediate level in Medical Maltese.
The learner will be able to:
a)	Practice the use of elementary to pre-intermediate medical vocabulary in the medical setting
b)	Practice the use of elementary to pre-intermediate Maltese grammar to help him/her communicate in a medical context
c)	Demonstrate good understanding of the Maltese culture related to the Medical Sector
d)	Practice establishing and maintaining social contact
e)	follow instructions in Maltese and complete successfully a range of well-defined tasks related to medical procedures and practices By the end of the course learners would be expected to 

a)	recall an elementary to pre-intermediate vocabulary related to thematic areas related to the medical environment/sector
b)	Revise and consolidate further the appropriate use of Maltese grammar in relation to medical terminology/ environment. Amongst others:
a.	Describe meaning and appropriate use of adjectives (including comparative & superlative) in relation to medical terminology
b.	Recall meaning and the appropriate use of more nouns related to the medical sector
c.	Revise the use of pronouns including attached pronounce related to medical scenario
d.	Recall meaning and appropriate use of conjugation in the present and past tense of frequently used verbs in the medical scenarios and forming the negative
c)	Recall number and fractions for the administration of medicine
d)	Get a more detailed insight of the Maltese culture related to the Medical Sector. Topics include:
•	Triage system at the emergency department
•	Security in hospitals
•	Current health issues in Malta
•	My Health Portal https://myhealth-ng.gov.mt/
•	Maltese Healthcare for Foreigners
•	European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) & Non-EU citizens This module/course is mainly designed for learners who would like to obtain an elementary to pre-intermediate knowledge of Medical Maltese. They will:
a) possesses good knowledge of the general medical vocabulary, anatomical terminology and scientific terminology
b) have a good understanding, are aware and interpret general colloquial expressions for medical terms
c) have the ability to use language for medical purpose
d) have a good understanding of the patients’ general symptoms
e) have a good command of the basics of Maltese grammar and syntax
f) get a more detailed insight of the Maltese culture

title: Dry Stone Wall Restoration (Restawr tal-Hitan tas-Sejjieh)
description:
This practical course will equip learners to set out,  construct and finish a traditional rubble wall using a variety of building stones and traditional lime mortars. The importance of laying the stones correctly and the use of pinning stones will be emphasised so that no more than 30% of the volume of the wall is mortar.
Demonstrate dry wall construction techniques using appropriate tools and necessary safety precautions; Identify PPE to be used during the construction of dry walls at various rural/ surrounded by build-up areas; Carry-out a field study on an existing wall or building recording such information as the time wall was constructed,  the type of wall,  the type of stone etc; Set out using profiles and build a dry stone wall to given dimensions and specifications; Select stone that is suitable for building walls; Prepare stone to include cutting and dressing rubble stone leaving it ready for wall construction; Use a given plan to construct and erect profiles,  set out and build a coursed mortared rubble wall to include building an suitable coping of stone over the length of the wall; Use a given plan and instructions to construct and erect profiles,  set out and build a mortared random rubble uncoursed wall to include a suitable coping of stone to the tope and length of the wall; Carry out stonewall construction under supervision and in accordance with appropriate health and safety procedures. Define dry wall construction terminology; List the different type of tools used for dry wall construction; Outline the main types of traditional stonewall construction to include common features; Identify stone the three main categories of stone used in traditional stonewall construction to include the advantages for each; Read plans for traditional stonewall construction to include interpreting measurements and terminology; Set up profiles for the excavation and building of a stone foundation,  to include explain why stone projects past the wall width and why larger stones are used

title: Foundation Certificate in Hairdressing,  Beauty and Well-Being
description:
This programme of studies provides learners with an overview of the different routes,  particularly in the areas of Hairdressing and Beauty,  which are available at Level 3 after completion of this course. The modules on offer provide learners with basic knowledge in health and safety practices employed during beauty and hairdressing techniques and procedures. Other modules focus on an understanding of the basic scientific concepts related to all hair and beauty services and treatments; and an introduction to basic business concepts. The course also provides learners with quality work experience exposure where they will be expected to assist and carry out a range of assigned tasks,  using approved models. Learners are required to purchase the necessary hairdressing and beauty accessories at the beginning of the academic year.
Understand the basic business concepts required to run a micro business. title: Award in Assistant Excavation Operative
description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety operating and working practices and will lead the learner to acquire the competence to be able to become an assistant excavation operative in the building and construction sector. The candidate shall be able to use the knowledge and skills to work effectively with superiors and colleagues using small portable powered tools 

The overall objectives of the course are also to encourage employees to adhere to use safe working practices in the building and construction sector. It is also intended to make candidates aware of the skills, knowledge or competences these may already possess while seeking further education to fill training gaps the candidate might need to have a safer building and construction environment in the sector.
The learner will be able to: 

Be able to keep up to date with legislation updates The learner will be able to: 

	Communicate with superiors and colleagues or site managers
	Communicate using simple glossary terms used in the building and construction.
	Communicate using basic Maltese or English
	Use appropriate nonverbal communication

title: Award for Assistant Excavation Operatives
description:
The unit helps familiarize the learner with legal responsibilities related to Health and Safety issues and to contribute to a safer work place by identifying hazards,  taking appropriate action to reduce any risks involved and follow good procedures in case of injury or ill health.  The learner will acquire the skills required to identify,  locate and protect sub-structures and utility services before and during excavation. This includes the use of tools and electronic detecting equipment.The unit also covers basic understanding of portable powered tools and plants,  and their correct operation.  The learners will know how to use the correct procedure to manually excavate around utility services by selecting the correct tools and equipment.  The safe and correct method to backfill and reinstate a surface will also be demonstrated.
Identify services and sub structures at the workplace whilst assisting in protecting these services when working around them. Contribute to Health and Safety requirements at the workplace. Assist in manually excavating and reinstating excavated surfaces and trenches to the required finishes. Operate portable powered plant and equipment at the workplace.

title: Award in Health and Safety and Planning Procedures in Marine and Diving Works
description:
Participants will acquire knowledge about safe diving practices to be adopted in operations in which persons are employed to work underwater. Participants will acquire competencies about safe marine and diving works and related supporting safe work practices conducted in connection with all types of work in a marine environment, for land-based construction work carried out on, adjacent to or over water and underwater.
Define the responsibilities of employees, contractors and supervisors working in marine-related sectors. Become acquainted with diving modes and competences of divers. Be acquainted with procedures and permits to work are required in a port area and in places close to the shore but outside the designated port areas. Define safety planning requirements on a marine-related workplace. Identify warning symbols and safety signs related to health and safety in marine-related workplaces. Demonstrate an understanding of potential hazards in marine-related workplaces and appropriate responses. Apply health and safety procedures in marine-related workplaces. Demonstrate an understanding of how to comply with regulations concerning health and safety in the marine environment at the national level and how follow the best practices that are used at the international level in this particular work environment.

title: VET Award Foundation in Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) Welding

Through this training programme,  the learner will be conversant with OHS requirements for welding environments and will be able to select suitable techniques to produce basic welded joints using TIG technology.
Quote health and safety procedures and practices specific to working with working with Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Describe health and safety measures and precautions to prevent hazards and to ensure the safety of oneself and third parties when working  in welding environments. Practice welding tee fillet joints in the flat position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Practice welding tee fillet joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Practice welding corner joints in the flat position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment.

title: Award in General Intensive English Course as a Foreign Language at Pre-Intermediate Level
description:
This Award course is designed to enhance and upgrade the participants’ spoken,  written,  reading and English listening skills through inputs of several different topics for discussion,  analysis and critical thinking.    Learning and recycling of grammar and vocabulary will occur through contextually interactive activities that will encourage learning. The programme is delivered over 4 weeks where each key area of Speaking,  Reading,  Listening & Writing is explored with the support of interactive lectures,  video discussions,  exercises,  individual and pair working together with role plays activities.  The whole programme is highly interactive and it is expected to enrich the participants’ knowledge in key all areas; sharpen their skills; and enhance their English competence.
Through the communication skills of speaking,  writing and listening,  the course will aid the students to be better able to; deal with common situations when in an English speaking country,  talk about family,  hobbies,  work,  travel and current events,  talk about experiences and events,  dreams,  hopes and ambitions,  give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans,  narrate and criticise a summary of a story from a book or film,  ask personal questions,  give and ask for directions,  talk about different personalities,  make and organise travel arrangements,  confidentally order in a restaurant,  talk about likes and dislikes,  express preferences,  make deductions and predicitions,  make offers and suggestions,  talk about obligation. At the end of the program,  the learner will be able to; Speak more fluently but accurately,  use the correct lexical jargon needed for different contexts,  use the correct grammar correctly when speaking about different contexts such as,  families,  restaurants and entertainment activities,  talk about personalities and characteristics,  giving and reading biographies,  describe Buildings,  monuments in terms of design,  texture and materials,  prediction of weather,  describe and talk about clothes and accessories,  pronounce and talk about large numbers,  be conversant with terms and phrases related to travel and tourism,  be conversant with phrases related to work and careers,  describe and talk about various hobbies,  sports and interests,  talk about the importance of Education and the benefits,  life changes and events,  talk about and criticise political beliefs,  systems and change,  talk about animals,  their extinctions,  habitats,  environment and rights,  descriptions of people,  health,  fitness and illnesses, types and likes / dislikes of music and concerts,  describe use and benefits of of household equipment.

title: VET Award as Assistant Plumber
description:
Provides the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as a Plumber’s Assistant. This course will enable the learner to acquire the basic knowledge, skills and competences of domestic plumbing installations,  routine maintenance and repair. Persons following this course will be able to assist in the repair,  maintenance or installation of domestic plumbing installations. Furthermore,  the learner will know how to mitigate health and safety concerns at work.
Report any hazards which may present risk to other persons. Seek expert assistance when help is needed. Explain the correct procedure for setting out domestic pipe work systems. Explain how to use and maintain pipe bending equipment. Explain how to use and maintain pipe threading equipment. Name the types of pipe,  fittings and jointing systems used for sanitary pipe work. Keep up to date with any changes made in the Maltese Occupational Health and Safety Act 2000. Keep up to date with any changes made to the National Occupational Standards published by MFHEA.

title: VET Award as Assistant Tile Layer
description:
Provides the learner with foundational knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as assistant tile layers. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to follow health and safety procedures and will achieve basic skills in laying floor and wall tiles,  both for internal areas and outside areas surrounding buildings,  under supervision.
Discuss in an active manner during class sessions and workshop sessions to ensure clear understanding of what is being taught. Interact with trainer and other learners in order to ensure understanding of others point of view. Illustrate good communication skills by applying the appropriate gestures and tones. Take an appropriate approach to study in order to learn how to select information and apply it to the task at hand. Study and keep up to date with safety features of new equipment and tools used by the trade.

title: VET Award in Principles of Plumbing
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as a Plumber’s Assistant. This course will enable the learner to acquire the basic knowledge and skills of domestic plumbing installations,  routine maintenance and repair and will be able to assist in the repair,  maintenance or installation of domestic plumbing installations Furthermore the learner will know how to mitigate health and safety concerns at work.
Show how to safely manually handle heavy loads. Apply appropriate procedures to contact personnel who are designated to deal with emergency situations. Prepare pipes that are appropriate for a given domestic plumbing project. Demonstrate how to chase through brick and stone for the plumbing services. Practice assembling and fitting metal fittings such as tees,  elbows,  bushes,  sockets and reducers for a plumbing task. Assemble and fit appropriate water pumps for roof and well installations. Identify health and safety procedures related to domestic plumbing environments. Describe how hazards and risks are assessed in domestic plumbing environments. Identify different metal fittings,  such as tees,  elbows,  bushes,  sockets and reducers,  used in various domestic plumbing projects.

title: Award in Industrial Relations
description:
As a result of this course,  the participants will benefit directly from the training provided since they will be trained in a number of areas which can help them to improve and enhance their representative skills and their relations with other workers. In return,  this would contribute towards ensuring that social dialogue is more effective
The course will provide participants with outcomes related to industrial relations in the following areas: the labour market; inustrial relations; health and safety at the workplace; intra-personal and occupational skills; case studies and english The learner will be able to communicate the knowledge gained through their improved and enhanced leadership skills and their team work relations with other workers; comment and engage in professional discussions concerning social dialogue and industrial relations; listen and communicate effectively in the particular working and social environment and communicate sound arguments/cases through sound listening skills The students will learn to identify the main grounds of discrimination at work,  discuss the importance of group roles,  learn how to communicate effectively,  give presentations and work in a group.  They will also learn to perceive the basic aspects the basic aspects of the collective bargaining process and also summarize the employees' feedback regarding proposals and issues related to industrial relations

title: Health and Safety Legal Responsibilities of the Employer
description:
This course is designed to  provide participants with the skills and confidence  to meet the requirements of the guidelines and regulations,  relating to the management of the safety of the workplace and the documentation required.
Be aware of what constitutes a suitable and sufficient risk assessment and who is considered competent person to carry out such tasks. Effective ways of examining workplace conditions to make sure they conform to applicable standards. Designing,  providing and maintaining a safe place of work that has safe access and egress,  and uses plant and equipment that is safe and without risk to health. Determining the type of H&S signs the workplace needs,  according with the existing hazards and understand how to use them. Determining the type of approach needed to properly to cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives in the event of an emergency in workplace. Applying procedures to prevent and minimize safety risks. Applying safety controls to manage residual risks. Managing the H& S file An understanding of the role,  functions and responsibility of the employer. An understanding of what kind of legal responsibilities apply to the management of a work place. Identifying of key elements for effective risk management in the workplace. Understanding the correct method to manage prevention measures that can be taken to minimize risk in a workplace. Sound knowledge of the correct method to manage the procedures to be followed in case of emergency. The need for fire safety and implementation of measures to protect yourselves,  employees and clients. Knowledge of H&S in workplace topics (i.e. personal protective equipment,  youn workers,  lift regulations,  back injury regulations,  accident reporting). Knowledge of common types of evacuation procedures and the control of personnel. Analyse and understand some court decisions,  both local and international,  to cast light on what is reallt expected from employers in workplaces. Maintain their knowledge up to date by linking and directing them to leading bodies in H&S,  both locally and internationally Manage emergency procedures and the control of personnel; Instruct personnel to prevent health and safety hazards at work; Identifying legal requirements from employers; Implement measures to protect all staff including third parties; Manage emergency procedures and the control of personnel; Maintain continuous professional development

title: Award in Safe Use of Electrical Hand Held Apparatus
description:
This course is designed for those workers who need to work on electrical equipment who either have no electrical qualifications or need a reminder of electrical dangers and safe working practices. This course provides knowledge and skills on electrical and mechanical hazards, on the functioning of portable tools and on the safety procedures to use at workplace.
Know the general site safety, particularly from the point of view of electrical hazards. Understand the electrical and mechanical hazards that can be encountered using an electrical tool and the precautions to be taken. Know technical and organisational preventive measures relevant to electrical and mechanical hazards in the use of electrical hand held apparatus. Know how identify and report faulty portable electrical equipment and withdraw it from service, by ensuring it cannot be used and/or is marked faulty. Perform a basic risk assessment to identify the hazards specific to electrical safety, the risks arising from those hazards, and the control measures you should use. Achieve a visual inspection that should be carried out by the user each and every time the equipment is used, checking for example for evidence of damage, loose cables etc. Determine the type of approach needed to comply with safe work procedure. Apply procedures of operational maintenance. Cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives in the organisation of an electrical emergency in workplace.

title: VET Award in Plastering
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as a Plasterer. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to identify and understand how to mitigate health and safety concerns at work and the correct methodologies to be able to prepare inside and outside walls for plastering,  plaster and finish off.
Define what constitutes hazards and what constitutes risks at the workplace. Describe how hazards are marked. Describe how to measure and calculate from plans to select materials. Define the processes and procedures of plastering. Define how to take actual measurements from plans and carry out calculations on quantities of material. Define how to calculate quantities to assist in preparing,  costing and estimating material used in plastering. Apply appropriate reporting procedures to bring hazards to the attention of designated personnel. Practice handling various hazardous materials on a work site in accordance with health and safety procedures. Demonstrate the basic properties of the main types of plastering materials in use. Practice using the appropriate tools and equipment for a given plastering task. Plan what materials,  equipment and tools are required for a plastering task. Operate using appropriate methods in indoor plastering according to the context.

title: Safe Handling of Chemicals for Manual Labourers

description:
