description:
Styling hair by different methods is a basic and necessary skill that is an important part of the hairdressing profession
Various styling tools,  their use and maintenance; hair structure in relation to water and heat; various styling and setting products and their use in styling and shaping hair and hair types and its texture density and thickness and growth pattern The learner will be able to style and dress hair using vairous tools,  products and methods; finger dry hair,  shape hair and blow dry hair; style hair in modern,  classic and elegant styles; use products and tools to create and maintain the styles and care for tools and equipment used in styling etc Produce styles on different types of hair using different methods,  tools and products after adequate consultation; style hair according to the client's wishes and to suit the occasion; use products and tools to produce such styles; provide after care and mantain health and safety throughout all procedures

title: Award in Legal,  Regulatory and Organisational Requirements of a Contact Centre
description:
This module concerns understanding an organisation’s procedures for dealing with legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements in a contact centre and the legal,  regulatory and ethical limits of contact centre work.
Define health and safety procedures in a contact centre. Explain the difference between a risk and a hazard in the workplace. Describe an organisation’s procedures for raising legal,  regulatory and ethical concerns. Describe internal and external sources of information on legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements. Interpret an organisation’s procedures for dealing with legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements in a contact centre. Identify the legal,  regulatory and ethical limits of contact centre work. Explain the importance of following health and safety procedures to minimise risk. Summarize the scope of legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements in a contact centre. Identify how the legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements relate to a contact centre. Explain how an ‘ethical approach’ affects a contact centre.

title: Award in Demolition Operative (with licence to operate small mobile plants)
description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety working practices and acquire the competence to be able to operate small mobile plants in the building and construction sector. The candidate shall be able to use further knowledge and skills to operate effectively under supervision using small mobile plant equipment on construction sites for demolition
Carry out research on the subject and units for this award. Carry out safe working practices. Find an appropriate way to reflect and evaluate their own work; seek advice,  information and support when appropriate. Communicate with colleagues and supervisors or site managers. Communicate using simple glossary terms used in the building and construction. Communicate using basic Maltese or English. Use appropriate nonverbal communication. Discuss work progress to supervisors.

title: VET Award in Life Skills for the Work Environment
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to gain and retain employment. Through this training programme,  the learner will be better trained and competent to use personal and social skills as well as customer care skills.
Apply learning skills and learning styles of self and others in a daily life context. Apply strategies to improve one's time management skills in a work and daily life context. Show shich aspects make up a customer care. Demonstrate how one can establish loyal customers. Identify one's learning skills and learning styles. Describe the advantages of possessing time management skills. Recall interpersonal communicative skills for the place of work. Identify verbal and non-verbal communication skills.

title: VET Award in Water Well Repair and Maintenance
description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work in the industry sector of water well repair and maintenance. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to safely identify faults in water well systems,  undertake or advise on corrective repair procedures,  and perform maintenance procedures on water well systems.
Quote  the main health and safety procedural standards used in the sector.  List  five hazards and risks associated with workplace activities. Recite mathematical calculations related to cylindrical,  spherical and cubic volume,  ratios and proportions. Describe how pressure gauges and basic hydraulics work. Write basic water chemistry formulae and equations used to perform water quality checks. Describe the main characteristics of modern water systems,  ranging from the operator’s duties to the filtration techniques that could be used for rain water. Recall that the proper function of the wellhead is to ensure that it is not allowing the entry of surface water or foreign materials. Recall that it is important that the well cap is firmly in place and that it can withstand the weight of persons and animals. Apply on-the-job health and safety best working practises to ensure the safety of one’s self,  the safety of other persons and due care for third parties’ property. Demonstrate proficiency when dealing with GHS chemical hazard warning symbols,  hazard warning,  emergency and mandatory signs. Operate water well equipment typically used for water well repair and maintenance – much better if the equipment is specifically mentioned. Demonstrate the liabilities and responsibilities related to the proper use of such equipment. Demonstrate the affects of the process of sedimentation on water quality.  Monitor the various appropriate water filtration techniques. Show the consequence of  signs of corrosion or deterioration of the well casing. Apply appropriate techniques when looking for signs of ground settling around the outside of the well casing.

title: Award in Housekeeping
description:
The course is intended to give learners the competencies to work proficiently as Housekeepers. This qualification will provide the necessary theoretical knowledge, practical skills and competencies for learners to apply housekeeping skills in workplace. The learner will be able to understand the overall processes for adequate housekeeping.
l) Illustrate the complexities and demands of working in the hospitality industry through the scope of housekeeping.
m) Recognise and demonstrate good work practices in the provision of housekeeping services.
n) Plan and use appropriate problem solving skills in order to provide the best service possible.
o) Use appropriate Health and Safety practices and infection control protocols to safeguard oneself, colleagues and customers. 
p) Recognise, prevent and react professionally to safety risks both for the customers and the workers.
q) Develop recommendations for improvement in the upkeep of premises. 
r) Understand, and apply reflectively and critically  the main ethical principles of housekeeping. 
s) Become aware of regulations and legisation in relation to housekeeping.  
t) Propose strategies for addressing challenges which might be encourtered at the work place.
u) Works as team-member within a multidisciplinary team.
v) Communicate professionally and clearly with customers, colleagues, subordinates and superiors. a) Understand facts and procedures related to high-quality, ethical houskeeping, meet houskeeping-related challenges and recommend improvements that could be implemented to emeliorate the service
b) Assess, evaluate and interpret the role of the housekeeping department in hotel operations
c) Apply knowledge and skills to be able to carry out housekeeping duties safely, following Health and Safety practices and infection control protocols to safeguard oneself, colleagues and customers. 
d) Apply knowledge and skills to be able to communicate effectively with the front office and the engineering and the maintanance division
e) Select and use relevant knowledge to identify the typical cleaning responsibilities of housekeeping and explain how  area inventory lists, frequency schedules are carried out and utilised. f) Understand and meet the challenges associated with the housekeeping department.
g) Understand the key issues of housekeeping.
h) Understand the theoretical and practical knowledge that constitutes the work of housekeeping.
i) Describe the role of the housekeeping department in hotel operations, 
j) Explain the importance of effective communication between housekeeping, the front office and the engineering and maintenance division.
k) Identify typical cleaning responsibilities of the housekeeping department, and explain how area inventory lists, frequency schedules are carried out.

title: Award in Poultry Production and Husbandry
description:
This unit is designed to give a good understanding of the principles of laying and broiler husbandry and production. It especially targets individuals who are interested in opening a new poultry farm or who would like to update their skills to manage better an already running poultry enterprise.  This unit�s sessions are delivered in class and on a working farm and the learner will be expected to spend various hours in practical sessions on the farm. The unit will go over the basic principles of farm design and poultry husbandry including feeding,  chicken health,  slaughtering,  egg grading lighting,  record-keeping,  animal welfare and the legislation regulating this sector.
Understand basic principles of the animals� farm life-cycle and farm structure/s to accommodate this cycle. Follow agreed procedures to harvest product. Undertake tasks to follow agreed feeding regimes. Explain methods that are utilized to prevent and cure diseases and parasite infections.

title: Award in Providing and Maintaining Administrative Services
description:
The module will strengthen the general skills previously gained through training and experience of the professional manner in which administration support is provided in the office environment.
Compile a skill scan relevant to their own role. Interpret the principles of SMART goals. Describe the typical services provided by your office in the workplace.,  including:  document production,  audio transcription,  data entry,  photocopying and binding,  document control,  filing/client records management,  stationery issue and stock control,  petty cash and expenses,  reception,  dealing with incoming/outgoing mail. Identify steps to ensure the smooth running of an event. Including: venue/location,  fees/cost,  catering and accommodation,  publicity/advertising,  equipment,  resources,  delegates/audiencepresenters/speakers,  joining instructions,  health,  safety and emergency procedures,  activities scheduled,  information. Use smart goals to develop a personal and professional development plan that is consistent with business needs and personal objectives. Demonstrate a thorough familiarity with the principles of offering administrative services,  in various workplace situations. Identify the importance of office procedures,  evaluating and identifying any gaps in their own office procedures. Monitor progress and agreed targets in the workplace,  applying techniques explored in this module. Plan an event in their workplace with confidence. Explore principles of personal responsibilities and how to develop and evaluate own performance at work. Apply skills gained to provide professional services to your office in the workplace. Interpret and comply with office management procedures. Apply techniques to monitor and manage work flows. Organise a simulated event in your workplace within a team.

title: Award in Healthcare

Practise in accordance with the relevant codes of professional conduct: standards for conduct,  performance and ethics,  within the limitations of the individual's own competence,  knowledge and sphere of professional practice,  consistent with the legislation relating to healthcare practice; Work collaboratively with other practitioners and agencies; Work effectively across professional boundaries and develop professional networks; Ensure privacy and dignity of individual throughout any activity and provide care and compassion in addressing individual’s needs and concerns;  Practice in a way,  which respects,  promotes and supports individual's rights,  interests,  preferences,  beliefs and cultures; Ability to assist others within the healthcare working environment Reflect on personal knowledge,  skills and practice for continuing professional development;  Understand personal role and responsibilities in providing care; Understand the legislation and standards governing person-centred care; Understand teh meaning and importance of person centred care; Describe how to promote choice and independence; Explain how to improve care delivered to ensure person centred care

title: VET Award for Call Centre Agents
description:
This course aims at providing the learner with general and comprehensive knowledge and skills necessary in the call centre environment. It is aimed at enabling the learner to demonstrate ability in performing good customer care skills and telephone techniques.
Understand the evolution and functions of call centre. Define the role of call centre. Understand call centre systems and technology. Use call centre systems and technology to carry out service requested by customer. Understand how the system administration within a call centre functions. Familiarise with the system security management. Identify how attitude affects interaction with customers. Know how to provide requested information about produce and/or service. Define process integration. Define a problem and identify steps on how to solve the problem. Identify the purpose of a call centre. Identify the key features of a call centre. Log into the system used within the call centre that is appropriate for dealing with customers. Use tools and techniques to edit,  process,  format and present information to the customers. Perform general duties of a call centre agent. Follow good working practices. Identify the difference between an assertive and angry customer. Show how to distinguish between reacting and responding to a difficult or angry customer. Operate the calls received in accordance with organisation's protocols or procedures. Demonstrate ability to solve a problem in an effective manner.

title: Award in Mental Health First Aid
description:
Those interested in mental health and supporting individual with mental health, either at the workplace or in every day life.
The learner will be able to: 

a)	Discuss the history of psychiatric care together with the differences it has accross different cultures
b)	Demonstrate knowledge of the different classifications of mental illnesses such as mood disorders, anxiety disorders, somatoform disorders, schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders
c)	Show knowledge of the different causes of mental illness such as genetics, environment, childhood trauma, negative thoughts, stress and stressful events, drugs, alcohol, unhealth habits and brain chemistry amongst others
d)	Demonstrate understanding of how to care for individuals who have acute symptoms and which might be unstable before admission to stabilisation
e)	Demonstrate awareness of sleep disorders, sleep hygiene, psychopharmacology in adults, depression, bipolar, anxiety disorders, dementia, psychosis and eating disorders in adults
f)	Identify early onset of symptomps of dementia through the assessment of behaviour 
g)	Demonstrate ability to recognise mental health emergencies such as agression, violence, self-harm, suicide
h)	Use de-escalation techniques in a mental health crisis 
i)	Identify instances of substance misuses such as druge use and abuse, alcoholism, use of opiods, stimulants, drugs, and any other addictions such as gambling and excessive digital use
j)	Demonstrate awareness of rights and legislations governing mental health, including the rights of mental health patients
k)	Identify the factors which demonstrate challenging behaviour  and mental illnesses in children and adoloscents
l)	Plan the approporiate care of the client through the assessment of health status
m)	Discuss the indications and the implementation of the various therapeutic modalities that can be implemented with child and adolescents The learner will be able to: 
a)	Recall the istory of psychiatry
b)	Describe the local situation with regards to mental health including prevalance, services, professionals, etc

title: Diploma in Electrical Installations
description:
This programme is the first stage for a learner who is interested in a career in electrical systems such as that of an Electrician within the construction industry. It contributes towards an understanding of the relevant theory and allows learners to develop the practical skills required in this field. The programme consists of twelve modules,  out of which six are vocational related and the rest are key skills related. Vocational modules focus on the basics of wiring electrical installation circuits using different cables and containment,  electrical installation regulations,  and health and safety requirements governing electrical installation processes. The rest of the modules provide an opportunity for learners to have adequate skills in Maltese,  English,  Mathematics,  Information Technology and Science and Technology.
Interpret and follow safety requirements in compliance with the law for electrical installations in construction environments Design and implement domestic electrical installations to given requirements Troubleshoot and repair existing single-phase electrical installation. Interpret wiring regulations and requirements for domestic electrical installations

title: Award in Sustainable Use of Plant Protection Products for Professional Users
description: In this course learners will be trained on the major legislation related to PPPs together with the risks and hazards related to handling,  use and storage of these products. The unit will then proceed to cover human and environmental health related to PPPs and how such products should be used safely and efficiently.

title: Award in Constant Watch
description:
The key purpose of constant watch or 24/7 observation is to provide a period of safety for patients during temporary periods of distress when they are at risk of harm to themselves and/or others. It is essential to ensure this period is therapeutic and that it is seen as a positive experience by the patient in time. It can also be used to provide an intensive period of assessment of a person's mental state. 
The purpose of this training programme is to develop participants knowledge and understanding of the clinical aspects involved in this process in order that they develop the competences and techniques to put into practice in 24/7 observation situations.

This Award has been created specifically for the needs of workers in the Health Care industry and will teach learners how to conduct 24/7 observation of patients in distress.
The learner will be able to:
a)	Demonstrate a range of techniques to assist individual in distress 
b)	Demonstrate a range of psychological and practical techniques for assisting individuals 
c)	Demonstrate techniques for the detection, de-escalation and management of aggression 
d)	Conduct a risk assessment on patient/individual Ensure environment for constant watch is safe
e)	 Practice patient centred care with awareness of patient privacy & dignity a)	Understand the relevant Mental Health legislation and regulatory framework
b)	Understand mental and psychiatric causes of mental distress
c)	Understand different levels of therapeutic observations
d)	Understand factors associated with self- harm / harm to others 
e)	Understand their role and responsibilities within healthcare team a)	Demonstrate knowledge of a range of clinical skills related to mental distress, anxiety and psychosis 
b)	Manage and engage people at risk of harming themselves or others
c)	Understand their roles and responsibilities as part of  a multi-disciplinary team in relation to supportive observations
d)	Carry out constant watch 24/7 observation within boundaries of role and according to care/treatment plan

title: Diploma in Welding and Fabrication

Identify materials and compare their properties Carry out Oxy-Acetylene Gas Welding,  Manual Metal Arc Welding and Metal Inert Gas Welding. title: Award in Delivery of Customer Service for Call Centres
description:
This module develops students’ knowledge of key concepts of Customer Care delivery. The module covers four subject areas including:Establishing a rapport with customers in a contact centre; Supporting customer service delivery; Delivering customer service; Demonstrating knowledge of customer service in contact centres
Identify precisely customers’ needs or requests. Check understanding of customers’ needs by summarising their queries and requests. Keep records of customer queries or requests in accordance with organisational procedures. Apply organisational guidelines to deal with customer queries or requests. Summarize the standards and procedures for dealing with incidents in a contact centre. Follow organisational guidelines for greeting and identifying customers. Explain the features and benefits of products and/or services to customers in accordance with organisational requirements. Provide the required information in response to customer requests. Check customers’ understanding of the information provided.  Identify options for the resolution of customers’ queries that meet their needs. Close the customer contact in accordance with organisational guidelines. Explain the basis on which incidents should be escalated. Identify regulatory requirements when dealing with customer contacts. Describe the sources of information to be checked in order to update knowledge and understanding of organisational and regulatory requirements. Describe the limitations of the service offer that can be made to customers. Describe the limits of authority in dealing with customers. Explain the importance of checking customers’ understanding of information provide. Explain the importance of closing a customer contact in a professional way in accordance with organisational procedures and standards. Describe the standards and procedures for handling incidents. Describe techniques for controlling conversations with contacts.
